evidence.description: Stored-credential retrieval suspends, then unconditionally applies credentials and marks the user logged in.
Credential renewal also applies its result unconditionally after suspension.
Logout clears authentication state, but does not invalidate pending authentication operations.
The user-info request suspends before assigning userProfile without verifying that the session is still current.

candidates.explanation: Actor isolation does not make operations atomic across await points. Credential retrieval and renewal apply their results without checking whether logout occurred while they were suspended. A pending operation can therefore restore tokens and set isLoggedIn to true after logout cleared them. Similarly, an outstanding user-info request can repopulate the profile after logout.
candidates.title: Suspended authentication operations can undo logout

evidence.description: The token-reset helper updates the main tokens and login flag but does not clear ssoCredentials.
Successful credential clearing uses that helper to reset authentication state.
Cookie creation checks only isLoggedIn before using the retained SSO credentials.

candidates.explanation: Logout clears the main tokens but leaves ssoCredentials intact. A subsequent login sets isLoggedIn to true without replacing those SSO credentials, and getSessionTokenCookie can immediately construct a cookie from the previous session's transfer token. This permits stale, potentially cross-account SSO state to survive a session change.
candidates.title: SSO credentials survive logout and subsequent login

evidence.description: Authentication state is reset only when clearCredentials returns true.
The failure branch throws only for a session error or renewable credentials; otherwise execution reaches the end of logout.

candidates.explanation: When clearCredentials returns false, no web-session error exists, and canRenewCredentials returns false, logout returns normally without clearing the in-memory tokens, login flag, or profile. Inability to renew does not establish that the existing in-memory authentication state has been cleared, so this path reports success while leaving that state untouched.
candidates.title: Logout silently succeeds on an unhandled credential-clearing failure

evidence.description: The throwing cache operation sits between resetting authentication tokens and clearing userProfile.
Profile-update notification is triggered by assigning userProfile, which the throwing path skips.

candidates.explanation: Image-cache clearing is awaited with try before userProfile is reset. If cache clearing throws, credentials and tokens have already been cleared, but the old profile remains and its update notification is not triggered. An ancillary cache failure therefore leaves logout only partially reflected in the service's state.
candidates.title: Cache-clearing errors prevent profile cleanup during logout

evidence.description: A false storage result throws credentialsStorageFailed, which is immediately caught and wrapped as credentialsStorageError.

candidates.explanation: The credentialsStorageFailed error thrown when storage returns false is inside the same do block whose catch wraps every error as credentialsStorageError. Consequently, callers never receive the distinct credentialsStorageFailed case from this path, despite the code explicitly attempting to distinguish a false result from a thrown storage error.
candidates.title: Credential-storage failure is caught and reclassified
